substory_punchline: Four reproducible microbiome ecotypes stratify Crohn's disease into biologically distinct patient groups

content.punchline: Four reproducible microbiome ecotypes stratify Crohn's disease into biologically distinct patient groups

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Deck opener — no prior section to lead in from; establish the stratification premise from a standing start. The argument this section makes: a four-ecotype framework exists, CD patients distribute across it non-randomly, and clinical covariates alone cannot recover the assignment. That three-part case is what earns the rest of the deck: ecotypes make confound-free target discovery possible, and targets make the cocktail framework possible.

content.title: Ecotype discovery: cMD pooling → cross-method consensus → UC Davis projection

nodes.label:
UC Davis projection
(23 CD patients onto K=4 LDA)

step_caption: Pool 8,489 curatedMetagenomicData MetaPhlAn3 samples; select K=4 by cross-method LDA×GMM adjusted Rand index local maximum
Commit a 2,417-alias synonymy layer (NCBI taxid + GTDB r214+ renames) as the project-wide species-reconciliation backbone
Project all 23 UC Davis CD patients onto the K=4 LDA embedding via the synonymy layer; ecotype call is LDA-primary, GMM advisory

slides.speaker_notes_seed: The pipeline has three non-trivial choices worth flagging for a methods-savvy audience. First: K=4 is selected by cross-method ARI between an LDA and a GMM on the same data — not by perplexity or BIC alone, which monotonically prefer larger K. Second: the taxonomy synonymy layer (2,417 aliases → 1,848 canonical species) is the backbone that makes multi-cohort pooling tractable; without it, Kaiju→MetaPhlAn3 projection for UC Davis would have ≈30% species-name mismatches. Third: UC Davis projection is LDA-primary; GMM is advisory because Kaiju↔MetaPhlAn3 classifier mismatch makes GMM calls fragile on that cohort. Source: REPORT §'Pillar 1 deliverables', NB01b, NB02.

content.subtitle: curatedMetagenomicData samples support a K=4 consensus ecotype framework (E0–E3)
content.sub_pointer: Cross-method ARI (LDA × GMM) selects K=4; LOSO ARI 0.113 (range 0.000–0.282) — a usable framework, not bit-reproducible across sub-studies
content.source_footer: REPORT.md §'Finding 1' (NB01b); NB04f LOSO stability; 5,333 HC + 3,156 IBD/other

slides.speaker_notes_seed: The headline is the sample scale: 8,489 cMD MetaPhlAn3 samples across multiple sub-studies, five diagnosis classes (HC, CD, UC, T1D/T2D, CDI). K=4 selected by cross-method ARI local maximum — a more honest criterion than BIC/perplexity. The four ecotypes align with published enterotype biology: E0 (66.8% of HC; F. prausnitzii / R. bromii), E1 (Bacteroides2 transitional; 48% CD, 58% UC), E2 (Prevotella copri; non-Western healthy), E3 (severe Bacteroides-expanded; 50% CD, 40% UC). The critical hedge: LOSO ARI 0.113 (range 0.000–0.282 across 8 sub-studies) shows real cross-study variance. Cluster boundaries shift with training-set composition. This is a usable operational framework, not a bit-reproducible classifier. A sharp reviewer will cite this; we surface it here rather than burying it. Source: REPORT.md §'Finding 1'; NB04f.

content.title: UC Davis CD patients distribute across three ecotypes non-randomly (χ²=10.0, p=0.019)
bullets: E0 27% / E1 42% / E3 31% / E2 0% — active-disease Western pattern; zero Prevotella-dominant patients
χ²(3) vs. uniform distribution = 10.0, p=0.019: non-random ecotype occupancy confirms stratification premise
73% of UC Davis patients fall in E1 or E3 — the two dysbiotic ecotypes with distinct pathobiont signatures

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This slide cashes the stratification premise: real CD patients from UC Davis don't fall uniformly across ecotypes. The χ² is against uniform — a conservative null. The absence of E2 is itself informative: E2 is the non-Western healthy Prevotella enterotype, essentially absent in active-disease Western CD cohorts. The 73% E1+E3 concentration (11 E1 + 8 E3 of 23) is what drives the cocktail design in S3 — nine E1 patients carry the full Tier-A pathobiont module. Ecotype breakdown: REPORT §'2. UC Davis CD patients span three ecotypes, none in E2'; χ² and p from REPORT §'Finding 2'; E0/E1/E2/E3 counts confirmed at REPORT §'Key Findings' table (E0=7, E1=11, E3=8). Transition cue: patients span the framework; now the question is whether clinical data alone can tell us which ecotype a patient is in — the next slide shows it cannot.

content.title: Clinical covariates reach AUC 0.80 but fail individual patients — metagenomics is required
left_col_content: Collapses to 'IBD → E1' on all-CD test cohort: is_ibd constant, classifier degenerates
Only 41% patient-level agreement with metagenomics on UC Davis
Extended classifier (+ HBI, SCCAI, calprotectin) reaches AUC 0.810 — marginal improvement
right_col_content: LDA projection onto K=4 embedding via synonymy layer
Per-patient ecotype call with confidence score (LDA primary)
Assigns all 23 UC Davis patients; confidence > 0.70 for majority
Distinguishes E1 vs E3 within CD — clinically meaningful divergence in pathobiont composition
Prerequisite for ecotype-specific cocktail design; cannot be replaced by chart data

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This slide makes the operational argument for why metagenomics is in the clinical workflow, not just the research workflow. The AUC 0.80 sounds strong, but it evaporates on a single-disease cohort: when the test set is all-CD patients, the 'is_ibd' feature is constant and the classifier collapses to predicting E1 for everyone. The 41% patient-level agreement with metagenomics is the operative number — coin-flip for individual patients. The E1-collapse failure mode is exactly the confound that motivates within-ecotype × within-substudy meta-analysis in S2. Source: REPORT §'3. Clinical covariates alone cannot assign IBD patients to ecotype'; NB03 minimal classifier. Closing hand-off to S2: ecotypes are real and CD patients occupy them non-randomly — but the framework has real cross-study variance (LOSO ARI 0.113). The operational question for S2 is whether the *targets* inside each ecotype replicate on a held-out cohort, even if the ecotype boundaries themselves shift. That is S2's opening line.
